title: V1 test, lane, and certification strategy, v1alpha1
description: Which test layer proves which public claim, in which execution lane, at what strength, and who owns the evidence. Certification level describes proof strength; the execution environment describes where the proof ran; the two are never conflated. A layer may not certify above the ceiling its evidence class allows, which is how a mock is prevented from certifying real runtime behaviour. Most rows are commitments for work that does not exist yet; v1Status says which is which, and a claim may cite evidence only once it is certified.

certificationLevels.name: Schema
certificationLevels.meaning: Documents, schemas, and inventories in this repository are internally consistent and validate. Nothing is executed against a runtime.

certificationLevels.name: Mock
certificationLevels.meaning: A consumer passes a deterministic contract suite against a labelled mock provider. It proves something about the consumer and the contract, and nothing about a provider.

certificationLevels.name: Real controlled
certificationLevels.meaning: A real provider works in a controlled, reproducible environment carrying an explicit environment label. The highest level V1 may claim.

certificationLevels.name: Failure
certificationLevels.meaning: Timeout, denial, unavailability, retry, and recovery are proven against a real provider. Out of V1 scope.

certificationLevels.name: Composed
certificationLevels.meaning: End-to-end integration across at least two real projects is proven. Out of V1 scope; there is no second project.

evidenceClasses.meaning: A statement in a document that nothing has run. It is the correct label for a design commitment and it certifies nothing at all.

A deterministic check over files in this repository: schema validation, fixture comparison, inventory consistency, link and whitespace checks. No network, no cluster, no model, no clock, no randomness.
A result produced against a labelled mock provider that loads no model.
A result produced against generated inputs or a simulated environment rather than the real one.
A number derived by calculation rather than measurement. It may inform a decision and may never certify one.
Executed on a contributor's own machine against the real component, on CPU, with versions and commands recorded.
Executed on authorized cloud CPU capacity against the real component, with provider, region, node shape, budget, and verified cleanup recorded.
Executed on authorized cloud GPU capacity against the real component, with the accelerator stack, allocation mode, budget window, and verified cleanup recorded. Not used anywhere in V1.

environments.repository-only: A checkout and a Python interpreter. No container engine, no cluster, no network, no model.
environments.local-kubernetes: The local kind cluster created by the environment scripts on a contributor's machine. No model is downloaded.
environments.capable-host: A host with the disk, memory, and time budget to hold the pinned model artifact and run the pinned runtime image. Either a contributor's machine following the documented manual procedure, or an explicitly labelled and authorized runner.

lanes.name: Default checks
lanes.purpose: Everything that can be proven from a checkout alone, run on every change, cheap enough that nobody is tempted to skip it.
prerequisites: Python 3.12 with pytest, jsonschema, and PyYAML
artifacts: the list of checks skipped and why
lanes.failureDiagnostics: The failing assertion, the identifier of the row or fixture that failed, and the exact command to reproduce it from a clean checkout. No lane-specific state is needed to reproduce a failure here, which is the point of the lane.
lanes.notes: Run by hand from CONTRIBUTING today. No continuous-integration lane is configured in this repository.

lanes.name: Cluster smoke
lanes.purpose: Prove that the local environment produces a working cluster and removes it again, without loading a model.
lanes.trigger: opt-in, on a change to the environment scripts, manifests, or chart
prerequisites: the host tier recorded in the prerequisites document
lanes.failureDiagnostics: Collected on failure into the ignored local artifacts directory: node and pod descriptions, events, and container logs. A failed run leaves the cluster in place for inspection and says so; teardown is a separate deliberate step.
lanes.notes: Executed once end to end on one Windows host by the environment scripts.

lanes.name: Real runtime
lanes.purpose: The only lane that may produce a C2 serving claim. It downloads the pinned model artifact, verifies its hash, and serves real inference.
lanes.trigger: manual, or an explicitly labelled and authorized capable runner
prerequisites: the disk headroom for the pinned model artifact, measured on the real backing volume rather than reported by df inside the cluster
the pinned model revision and its published per-file hash
explicit authorization to spend the time and, where a runner is paid, the money
artifacts: the resolved image digest and model revision
the computed and published artifact hashes
the request and response transcript with prompts and completions removed
lanes.failureDiagnostics: The stage that failed, named: download, hash verification, image pull, model load, readiness, request, or teardown. Model load and readiness failures additionally record the readiness endpoint's status over time, because a runtime that answers 503 while loading is correct readiness behaviour and wrong liveness behaviour, and the two are indistinguishable from a single sample.
lanes.notes: The documented manual procedure is the feasibility workflow, which has been executed once. No labelled runner exists.

lanes.name: Capacity
lanes.purpose: Sustained-load and capacity measurement. Defined so that the boundary around it is explicit, and deferred out of V1 unrun.
prerequisites: a hardware class the project is willing to name in public
a decision that publishing a capacity figure is in scope, which V1 has explicitly refused
lanes.failureDiagnostics: Not applicable; the lane is not run in V1.
lanes.notes: V1 may publish no throughput, latency, capacity, or benchmark figure. This lane exists in the strategy so that adding one is a visible decision rather than an accident.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of the published contracts and their rejection interface
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Keeps the schema, fixtures, and canonical refusals in step with what the validator actually does.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of the architecture records and the ownership inventory
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Keeps the committed boundary data and the documents describing it from drifting apart.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of the local development environment
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Keeps cluster creation, smoke, and teardown reproducible on a documented host tier.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of the serving runtime selection and its evidence
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Produces and maintains real-runtime records, and refuses to let a mock stand in for one.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of the platform domain, adapters, API, and deployment rendering
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Owns the tests for components that do not exist yet, and the claims they will have to support.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of the public-information boundary and secret handling
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Owns the scan configuration, the redaction rules, and the evidence that neither history nor telemetry carries something it should not.

evidenceOwners.name: The owner of published documentation and its verification
evidenceOwners.responsibility: Owns link, whitespace, and claim-accuracy checks over everything this repository publishes.

layers.name: Unit
layers.purpose: Exercise one domain rule in isolation, with no adapter, no cluster, and no runtime. The dependency rule exists so that this layer is possible at all.
layers.notes: The workload domain model is the first code this layer covers. It exercises domain objects with no adapter, no cluster, and no runtime, which is what the dependency rule exists to make possible. The rules that decide whether a contract is accepted are not implemented yet; the layer covers what parses, not what is valid.

layers.name: Contract and schema
layers.purpose: Validate the published schema, every valid and invalid fixture, and the exact refusal a consumer is given for each rule.
layers.notes: V1-S1-006-PR1 added the second path. The workload template renders a contract, and what it renders is held to the same schema and the same semantic rules as a committed fixture - by the same validator, not by a copy of it - so the checks belong to this layer rather than to a layer of their own.

layers.name: Architecture inventory
layers.purpose: Hold the committed ownership and component boundaries to their own rules: the inventory against the documents describing it, and the platform domain against the dependency rule that says what it may import.

layers.name: Serving adapter
layers.purpose: Prove that each adapter implements the interface the domain owns, including the mock adapter's obligation to identify itself as a mock.
layers.notes: An adapter suite runs against the interface, not against a runtime. Its ceiling is C1 even for the real adapter, because what it exercises is the shape of the call rather than the thing on the other end of it. The deterministic mock adapter is the first implementation it covers; the conformance suite it runs is inherited from tests/support/serving_conformance.py, which the in-memory double under the unit layer inherits as well.

layers.name: Mock integration
layers.purpose: Run the API end to end against the mock adapter: correlation propagation, canonical errors, redaction, and the not-ready path, deterministically and on every change.
layers.notes: This is the layer most at risk of being read as more than it is. It proves the consumer and the contract; it proves nothing about a provider. V1-S1-005-PR1 is what made it real: the API exists, and this layer drives it end to end against the labelled mock adapter and against controlled adapter doubles. V1-S1-005-PR2 closed its canonical-error obligation - the whole error body, every condition the accepted surface maps, and the configuration-driven adapter selection are exercised here. Two limits still travel with every result it produces. Nothing here crosses a socket - the API implements the ASGI calling convention, this repository ships no server, and the suites drive the application through its own interface - so a result establishes what the application decides and nothing about HTTP. And a row that composes the real adapter does so over a transport that refuses to be called, which establishes the shape of the composition and nothing about a runtime.

layers.name: Kubernetes smoke
layers.purpose: Prove the cluster half of the environment: a cluster is created, a workload is scheduled and answers, and teardown leaves no residue. No model is involved.
layers.notes: Real, and about the environment only. A cluster smoke result may never be cited in support of a serving claim.

layers.name: Real runtime smoke
layers.purpose: The only layer that may support a C2 serving claim: the pinned model artifact is downloaded and hash-verified, the pinned runtime image serves a real completion in a cluster, and the pod is removed.
layers.notes: Executed once, on one host, on one day, by the manual procedure; one pre-registered threshold was not met and the record says so. V1-S1-004-PR2 added an executable suite under tests/realruntime that drives the same runtime through the serving adapter, and V1-S1-005-PR2 added a second that drives it through the InferOps API composed from configuration. Neither has been run against a runtime: the lane is authorization-gated and was not entered, so the layer's cited evidence remains the manual trial.

layers.name: Failure and resilience
layers.purpose: Provoke the failures the architecture names as canonical errors — model not ready, runtime unreachable, timeout — against the real runtime rather than against an anticipated mock.
layers.notes: Full C3 failure certification — denial, retry, and recovery proven exhaustively — is out of V1 scope. What V1 needs from this layer is that each canonical error is produced by the condition it names.

layers.name: Capacity and load
layers.purpose: Sustained-load measurement. Defined and deferred, so that publishing a capacity figure requires deleting a deferral rather than adding a test.
layers.notes: V1 may publish no throughput, latency, capacity, or benchmark figure. The marker is registered and deselected by default so that a load test cannot arrive quietly in the default lane.

layers.name: Security scan
layers.purpose: Refuse a change that carries a credential, a model artifact, generated host state, or a personal filesystem path into public history.
layers.notes: A scan configuration and an allowlist are committed. No recorded run of the scanner exists, so this layer is planned rather than implemented, and the difference is deliberate: a configuration file is not a result.

layers.name: Documentation verification
layers.purpose: Prove that every relative link resolves, that no published document carries trailing whitespace or a hard tab, and that the machine-readable strategy and the documents describing it publish the same identifiers.
commands: the link and whitespace checks in CONTRIBUTING

claims.statement: Every document the validator refuses is refused with a canonical error code, a stable rule identifier, and a field location that the contract document publishes.
A change to any canonical code, rule identifier, or field location a consumer is given fails the build rather than passing as a refactor.
The committed ownership inventory assigns exactly one owner to every resource, and the Terraform and Helm sets do not intersect.
Every relative link in every published document resolves from the directory of the file containing it.
The machine-readable strategy and the documents describing it publish the same lane, layer, and claim identifiers in both directions.

No prompt, response, provider error body, or secret has any permitted placement in the committed telemetry catalog; a tenant identifier, a request-scoped identifier, and an unbounded or measured value are each excluded from a metric label, and a tenant identifier is excluded from a committed evidence record as well; and every metric stays inside a declared cardinality budget.

Every amount in the committed cost method declares a basis; only an invoice-backed basis may carry the vocabulary or the reference of an invoice; every unit cost carries the denominator it was divided by and is null below a declared minimum; every record's confidence is the lowest ceiling its own inputs allow rather than a value its producer asserted; and the worked example's amounts, shares, and unit costs are recomputed in exact decimal and close against the capacity they allocate.

Every control in the committed security baseline derives its status from the verification it names rather than asserting one; a control naming an automated test or a script guard names one that exists, and a control claiming an implemented status names an evidence record that is committed; no control claims to act inside a running system; every threat names a control or the deferred risk that carries it, and every recorded exception names a compensating control and its residual risk; every manifest this repository publishes is pinned by digest, carries eight pod-security assertions, and exposes no service outside the cluster; and the reserved vocabulary of a security posture appears in these documents only where it is denied.
The default lane downloads no model, and every marker belonging to a layer outside it is deselected by the committed pytest configuration.
The environment scripts create a working local cluster, schedule a workload that answers a request, and remove both with residue verified absent.
The pinned runtime image, holding the pinned model revision, answers a real inference request inside a Kubernetes cluster.

The downloaded model artifact's computed hash equals the hash published for the pinned revision, which is the whole of the integrity argument for a transfer whose downloader does not validate certificates.
A validated WorkloadContract document results in a deployed workload that answers an inference request through the platform API against the real runtime.
Chart values are produced from a validated domain object and from nothing else; no cluster object is read as the source of truth for a field the contract defines.
The mock adapter and every artifact it produces are identifiable as a mock from the artifact itself, not from the directory it sits in.
A request arriving while the runtime is still loading its weights returns the canonical model-not-ready error rather than a timeout, a restart, or a 503 the caller has to interpret.
The API stays healthy and returns the canonical unavailable error when the serving runtime cannot be reached, which is the failure mode the separate-deployment decision created.
No prompt, completion, credential, or unbounded identifier appears in a log line, a metric label, or a committed artifact.
The published history carries no credential, model artifact, generated host state, or personal filesystem path.
Installing and uninstalling one release leaves the prerequisite layer intact and leaves nothing of the release behind.
The platform sustains a stated request rate at a stated latency on a stated hardware class.
claims.deferralReason: V1 may publish no throughput, latency, capacity, or benchmark figure. Making one runtime work is not the same as engineering the runtime, and a capacity claim would be a claim about a runtime this project did not write.

evidenceRetention.certifyingRecords: A record that certifies a public claim is committed under docs/proof and retained for as long as the claim stands. It is retained in the repository's history rather than in a lane's artifact store, because an artifact store that expires cannot support a claim that does not.
evidenceRetention.laneArtifacts: A lane's raw output is retained for the period the lane declares and then expires. It exists to diagnose a failure, not to support a claim. Nothing may cite an expiring artifact as the evidence for a published claim.
evidenceRetention.promotion: Raw output that a claim depends on is promoted into a committed record before the lane's retention window closes, with prompts, completions, credentials, and host identifiers removed. A claim whose evidence was never promoted is uncertified, and the correct response is to rerun the lane.
evidenceRetention.supersession: A superseded record is kept and marked rather than deleted, so that a reader arriving from an old link finds the correction rather than a missing file.
